performance_optimizations.title: Optimize Products Page with Database JOIN Instead of Multiple Queries
performance_optimizations.description: The Products page (app/(dashboard)/products/page.tsx) executes 3 separate database queries sequentially: one for products, one for current_prices, and one for categories. These should be consolidated into a single query with JOINs or a Supabase select with nested relationships.
performance_optimizations.rationale: The current N+1-like pattern increases latency by requiring 3 round trips to the database. With 100+ products, this becomes a significant bottleneck. A single query with proper JOINs reduces network latency and database load.
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: 3 sequential database queries for products, prices, and categories
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: ~60-70% reduction in API call latency, single round-trip instead of 3
performance_optimizations.implementation:
1. Use Supabase's nested select syntax: .select('*, current_prices(*), categories(*)')
2. Or create a database view that joins products with current_prices and categories
3. Remove the manual mapping code that combines results
4. Update TypeScript types to match the new response shape
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: Supabase's nested selects may return slightly more data than needed, but the latency improvement outweighs this

performance_optimizations.title: Add React.memo to ProductListItem Component for Render Optimization
performance_optimizations.description: The ProductListItem component in the Products page is re-rendered for every item whenever parent state changes (search, filter, modal state). Wrapping it with React.memo would prevent unnecessary re-renders when product data hasn't changed.
performance_optimizations.rationale: Each state update (typing in search, opening modals) triggers a full re-render of all product list items. With 50+ products, this creates noticeable lag. React.memo ensures items only re-render when their props actually change.
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: All ProductListItem components re-render on any state change
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: ~80% reduction in unnecessary re-renders during search/filter operations
performance_optimizations.implementation:
1. Extract ProductListItem to a separate file
2. Wrap with React.memo
3. Use useCallback for the onEdit, onDelete, onToggleVisibility handlers
4. Consider virtualizing the list if product count exceeds 100
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: Slightly more complex component structure, but significant performance gain

performance_optimizations.title: Code Split Large Homepage into Lazy-Loaded Sections
performance_optimizations.description: The homepage (app/page.tsx) is 845 lines containing 15+ components (AnimatedBackground, AnimatedQRDemo, FeatureCard, StatCard, TestimonialCard, PricingTier, Navigation, Footer, etc.). These should be extracted and lazy-loaded for faster initial page load.
performance_optimizations.rationale: All components are bundled together, increasing initial JavaScript payload. Sections below the fold (testimonials, pricing, footer) can be lazy-loaded as the user scrolls, significantly reducing Time to Interactive.
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: Single 845-line file with all components bundled together
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: ~30-40% reduction in initial bundle size, faster LCP and TTI
performance_optimizations.implementation:
1. Extract each major section (Features, HowItWorks, Testimonials, Pricing, CTA) to separate component files
2. Use dynamic import with next/dynamic for below-fold sections
3. Add Suspense boundaries with skeleton loading states
4. Consider Intersection Observer for triggering loads
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: More files to manage, slight delay when scrolling to lazy-loaded sections

performance_optimizations.title: Optimize AuthProvider to Avoid Unnecessary Re-fetches
performance_optimizations.description: The AuthProvider (components/providers/auth-provider.tsx) performs 2 sequential database queries (organization_members, then organizations) on every auth state change. It also creates a new Supabase client on each render instead of memoizing it.
performance_optimizations.rationale: The sequential queries double the latency for auth initialization. Creating a new Supabase client on each render is wasteful and can cause issues with real-time subscriptions. These should be optimized for faster app initialization.
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: 2 sequential queries + new client creation on each render
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: ~50% faster auth initialization, reduced memory allocation
performance_optimizations.implementation:
1. Use useMemo to memoize the Supabase client creation
2. Combine the two queries using a JOIN: .select('*, organizations(*)')
3. Consider caching the organization data in localStorage for faster subsequent loads
4. Add error boundaries for auth failures
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: localStorage caching requires cache invalidation strategy

performance_optimizations.title: Add Virtual Scrolling for Long Product Lists
performance_optimizations.description: The Products page renders all products in a simple div with .map(). For restaurants with 100+ products, this creates DOM bloat and slow scroll performance. Implementing virtual scrolling would render only visible items.
performance_optimizations.rationale: Each ProductListItem creates multiple DOM elements (image, buttons, text). With 200 products, this means 1000+ DOM nodes. Virtual scrolling reduces this to ~20-30 visible items, dramatically improving scroll performance and memory usage.
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: All products rendered to DOM regardless of viewport visibility
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: ~90% reduction in DOM nodes for large product lists, smoother scrolling
performance_optimizations.implementation:
1. Install @tanstack/react-virtual or react-window
2. Wrap the product list with a virtualized container
3. Set fixed or estimated row heights for optimal performance
4. Handle dynamic row heights if product descriptions vary significantly
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: Adds dependency, slightly more complex list rendering code, fixed heights may require design adjustments
